sections.content: Advice expressions such as recomendar que, aconsejar que and ser importante que normally introduce the present subjunctive when the person receiving the advice is expressed as a separate subject. The subjunctive marks the recommended or desired action rather than presenting it as an established fact.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que descanses unos días.
items.english: I recommend that you rest for a few days.

items.spanish: El médico aconseja que bebas más agua.
items.english: The doctor advises that you drink more water.

items.spanish: Es importante que hagas ejercicio con regularidad.
items.english: It is important that you exercise regularly.

items.spanish: Te conviene descansar antes de volver al trabajo.
items.english: It is advisable for you to rest before returning to work.

sections.content: When the advice expression has que and introduces a different subject, use the present subjunctive: recomiendo que descanses. With the same subject, an infinitive is often more natural: te recomiendo descansar.
